subject.title: feat: add chain-of-thought pre-flight planning for long-running goals

question: Should OpenClaw expand session goals to own persistent model-mutable step plans and new goal-plan tools, or should long-running planning remain in the existing gated `update_plan` and Task Flow surfaces?
rationale: The patch changes durable session-goal shape, model-facing tool exposure, config defaults, prompt-cache placement, and reasoning-output policy, so automation cannot choose the product/API contract safely.

options.title: Pause for goal-plan API design
options.body: Keep this PR open but do not land until maintainers decide the permanent planning surface and update the implementation around that contract.

options.title: Repair behind existing gates
options.body: Proceed only if the new behavior is routed through the existing plan-tool policy or an approved Task Flow/goal-plan seam with schema, docs, upgrade proof, and real behavior proof.

options.title: Accept a new goal-plan contract
options.body: Maintainers may intentionally make goals own persistent step plans, but that needs explicit docs, migration expectations, retry semantics, and reasoning-output boundaries.

recommendation.title: Pause for goal-plan API design
recommendation.body: Keep this PR open but do not land until maintainers decide the permanent planning surface and update the implementation around that contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The central decision spans the `update_plan` feature history and core session-goal contract that this history most strongly ties to `steipete`.
